title: Your Credit Score, Explained in Numbers

lines.say: What actually moves your credit score?
Not your income, and not checking your own score. Here's what really counts, in numbers.

lines.cap: The common FICO score runs from 300 to 850, and it's built from five parts.
lines.say: The common FICO score runs from three hundred to eight fifty, and it's built from five parts.

scene.sub: What goes into a FICO score

lines.say: Payment history, thirty-five percent. Amounts owed, thirty percent. Length of history, fifteen.

lines.cap: New credit and credit mix make up the last 20%: 10% each.
lines.say: New credit and credit mix make up the last twenty, ten percent each.

scene.text: Autopay the minimum. Then pay more on purpose.

lines.cap: Payment history is the biggest piece. A payment 30 days late can stay on your report for up to seven years. The simplest fix: autopay at least the minimum on every card, then pay more by hand.
lines.say: Payment history is the biggest piece. A payment thirty days late can stay on your report for up to seven years. The simplest fix: autopay at least the minimum on every card, then pay more by hand.
Second, amounts owed, mostly your utilization.

lines.cap: Utilization is your balance divided by your limit. Our episode one card has $3,200 on a $5,000 limit: 64%.
lines.say: Utilization is your balance divided by your limit. Our episode one card has thirty-two hundred on a five thousand dollar limit. Sixty-four percent.

lines.cap: Lower is better. Under 30% is a common guideline, and under 10% is even better.
lines.say: Lower is better. Under thirty percent is a common guideline, and under ten is even better.
Here's the paycheck plan from episode one, month by month.
By month five, it's under thirty percent. By month eight, zero. Paying down debt helps your score as a side effect.

scene.head: THE OTHER THREE
items: Length: keep your oldest card open
Mix: never borrow just for this

lines.say: Length of history: keep your oldest card open, even if you barely use it. New credit: each application can mean a hard inquiry, so space them out. Credit mix matters least. Never borrow just to improve it.

scene.text: Checking your own score doesn't hurt it.

lines.cap: And checking your own score or report doesn't hurt it. You can get free reports at AnnualCreditReport.com.
lines.say: And checking your own score or report doesn't hurt it. You can get free reports at AnnualCreditReport dot com.
